To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

time changed Levy processes can be used to model the three key features of asset returns, namely jumps, time varying volatility, and negative correlation between volatility and returns, and that these processes are useful in pricing options.

the characteristic function approach to time changed Levy processes is the most general option pricing model available, that it encompasses almost all of existing option pricing literature, that the model is easy to implement and to test, and that the model can be used to price options on any asset class.
the time changed Levy processes are a general framework for option pricing that can simultaneously address the issues of jumps, volatility dynamics, and return volatility correlation.

the following question: What is the appropriate return process to use in the Black-Scholes option pricing model?
the pricing of options in the presence of stochastic volatility and jumps.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the time changed Levy process option pricing framework encompasses all existing option pricing models and it is a powerful tool for the pricing of options on a variety of underlying assets.

the Levy processes are more flexible and realistic than the Brownian motion, in the sense that they can model the price of the stock and the volatility of its price simultaneously and they can model jumps and the correlation between the stock price and its volatility.
the time changed Levy processes can be used as a general framework to study option pricing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that time changed Levy processes are a natural extension of the Black Scholes model.

the time changed Levy process is a very general model that is flexible enough to accommodate almost all of the features observed in option markets, but it is still parsimonious enough to be tractable and implementable.
the option pricing model we propose can simultaneously address the three important issues that are ignored in the classic Black-Scholes model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Black Scholes option price is an upper bound for the option price under almost every other model.
time changed Levy processes are a powerful tool for modeling and analyzing option prices.
